id: system-axes
title: "System axes — the six categorical strata of a FARS record system"
type: term
defines: system-axes
date-created: 2026-04-05
description: "A FARS record system is organized across six categorical axes, each with its own morphisms. Every record belongs to exactly one axis; cross-axis content is encoded as references between records."
instance-of: architectural-schema
axes: [work-axis, predication-axis, agency-axis, observation-axis, capability-axis, memory-axis]
purity-rule: "each record-type lives on exactly one axis; content that would cross axes is extracted to a referenced record on its proper axis"
related: [work-axis, predication-axis, agency-axis, observation-axis, capability-axis, memory-axis]
readiness: shaped
source-session: 246e6d58
---

A FARS record system is a composition of six distinct categorical structures, each organizing a different kind of content. The axes are not a hierarchy — they are orthogonal strata that interact via well-typed cross-axis morphisms.

**The six axes:**
- [work-axis](work-axis.md) — teleology chain from charter to event (what must happen)
- [predication-axis](predication-axis.md) — terms and specs (the vocabulary and its rules)
- [agency-axis](agency-axis.md) — offices, officers, roles (who acts)
- [observation-axis](observation-axis.md) — analyses, decisions, directives (claims about state)
- [capability-axis](capability-axis.md) — skills, commands, hooks, agents (executable terms)
- [memory-axis](memory-axis.md) — memories, instincts, feedback (persistence across sessions)

**Purity rule:** each record-type has a canonical axis. A plan is work-axis. A term is predication-axis. An analysis is observation-axis. When a record accumulates content whose axis differs from its own, that content extracts to a separate record on its proper axis, referenced via a cross-axis morphism.

**Axis crossings produce bloat.** When a plan tries to also carry its own spec (predication-axis), its architectural rationale (observation-axis), and its deployment how-to (capability-axis) all in one file, the prose grows to shift the reader between axes. Extracting each to its own record, linked by references, restores the record's axis-purity and compresses its body.

**Cross-axis morphisms** are named in each axis's term-definition. Typical patterns: `conforms-to` (work → predication), `assigned-to` (work → agency), `analyzed-by` (work → observation), `implemented-by` (work → capability), `informed-by` (work → memory).

This schema is derived from work-session 246e6d58 (2026-04-05) observing why large plan files bloat and grounding the resolution in the library's adjoint-predication math, work-ontology, and office theory.
"}

related: [work-axis, predication-axis, agency-axis, observation-axis, capability-axis, memory-axis]
readiness: shaped
source-session: 246e6d58
---

A FARS record system is a composition of six distinct categorical structures, each organizing a different kind of content. The axes are not a hierarchy — they are orthogonal strata that interact via well-typed cross-axis morphisms.

**The six axes:**
- [work-axis](work-axis.md) — teleology chain from charter to event (what must happen)
- [predication-axis](predication-axis.md) — terms and specs (the vocabulary and its rules)
- [agency-axis](agency-axis.md) — offices, officers, roles (who acts)
- [observation-axis](observation-axis.md) — analyses, decisions, directives (claims about state)
- [capability-axis](capability-axis.md) — skills, commands, hooks, agents (executable terms)
- [memory-axis](memory-axis.md) — memories, instincts, feedback (persistence across sessions)

**Purity rule:** each record-type has a canonical axis. A plan is work-axis. A term is predication-axis. An analysis is observation-axis. When a record accumulates content whose axis differs from its own, that content extracts to a separate record on its proper axis, referenced via a cross-axis morphism.

**Axis crossings produce bloat.** When a plan tries to also carry its own spec (predication-axis), its architectural rationale (observation-axis), and its deployment how-to (capability-axis) all in one file, the prose grows to shift the reader between axes. Extracting each to its own record, linked by references, restores the record's axis-purity and compresses its body.

**Cross-axis morphisms** are named in each axis's term-definition. Typical patterns: `conforms-to` (work → predication), `assigned-to` (work → agency), `analyzed-by` (work → observation), `implemented-by` (work → capability), `informed-by` (work → memory).

This schema is derived from work-session 246e6d58 (2026-04-05) observing why large plan files bloat and grounding the resolution in the library's adjoint-predication math, work-ontology, and office theory.

id: predication-axis
title: "Predication axis — terms, specs, and the vocabulary DAG"
type: term
defines: predication-axis
date-created: 2026-04-05
description: "The axis of terms and specs — the vocabulary in which all other records are written, and the invariants those records must satisfy."
instance-of: categorical-axis
part-of: system-axes
objects: [term, spec, primitive-term]
internal-morphisms: [presupposes, specializes, defines, constrains]
structure: "directed graph of predicate-definitions; presupposes builds a DAG among predicates; primitive-terms close the definition cycle"
cross-axis-morphisms:
  to-work: [serves, scopes]
  to-agency: [signatures-for-office]
  to-observation: [settled-by, established-by]
  to-capability: [grounded-in-term]
  to-memory: [grounds-predicate]
math-lineage: "Curry-Howard-Lambek correspondence (predicate=type=object-in-CCC); adjoint paper; hyperdoctrine structure; voidmath finite-F7 residuation"
related: [system-axes, work-axis, observation-axis]
readiness: shaped
---

Objects on this axis are predicate-definitions and invariant-sets. A **term** defines one predicate (what key means, its signature, its presuppositions). A **spec** is a bundle of invariants that some other record must satisfy. Primitive terms are those whose own definitions use only keys defined by other primitives — they close the meta-circularity.

Internal morphisms:
- **presupposes** — predicate B is meaningfully present only if predicate A is (e.g., `blocked-by` presupposes `status: blocked`)
- **specializes** — predicate B is a refinement of predicate A (e.g., `work-type: procedure` specializes `work-type: *`)
- **defines** — a term-record is the definition of its predicate
- **constrains** — a spec says a record of type T must satisfy these invariants

**Cross-axis extractions** — content that APPEARS in a predication-axis record but belongs elsewhere:
- rationale for choosing this definition → [observation-axis](observation-axis.md) via `settled-by:` or `established-by:` decision
- the implementation that enforces the invariant → [capability-axis](capability-axis.md) as a validator hook
- plans to fix violations → [work-axis](work-axis.md) via `serves:` on a plan

A term's body carries the definition prose (this is predication-axis's primary content). A spec's body states invariants (one per list-item in `invariants:` frontmatter), with body used only for clarifying examples.

See also: [system-axes](system-axes.md), [work-axis](work-axis.md), [capability-axis](capability-axis.md).
"}

id: agency-axis
title: "Agency axis — offices, officers, and deontic profiles"
type: term
defines: agency-axis
date-created: 2026-04-05
description: "The axis of normative positions and the persons filling them. Offices persist; officers occupy. Deontic profiles (powers, duties, privileges, immunities) govern what work an office may accept."
instance-of: categorical-axis
part-of: system-axes
objects: [office, officer, incumbent, role, assignment]
internal-morphisms: [delegates-to, reports-to, filled-by, installed-in]
structure: "presheaf on offices: each office determines a deontic profile; officers are sections (incumbents of offices) at specific times"
cross-axis-morphisms:
  to-work: [takes-assignments-from, owns]
  to-predication: [requires-capabilities-from, signature-of-duty]
  to-observation: [acted-in, attributed-to]
  to-capability: [uses-skill, permitted-commands]
  to-memory: [holds-memory, carries-instinct]
math-lineage: "Hohfeldian correlatives; Kantorowicz body-politic/body-natural; presheaf-on-offices from formal-structure-of-office; library/.../work/terms/office.md"
related: [system-axes, work-axis, capability-axis, library/.../work/terms/office.md]
readiness: shaped
---

Objects on this axis are normative positions (offices), persons filling them (officers/incumbents), and the acts that bind tasks to agents (assignments). An **office** persists independently of any holder. An **officer** is an incumbent bound to an office's deontic profile for the duration of occupancy.

An office's deontic profile declares: `action-domain`, `duties`, `autonomous`, `delegates-to`, `reports-to`, `escalates`, `filled-by-role`. These are the Hohfeldian coordinates — powers (what the office can do), duties (what it must do), privileges (what it may do), immunities (what it cannot be forced to do).

Assignment is the cross-axis morphism from work-axis to agency-axis: `task.assigned-to: <office>` creates the relation that makes an office responsible for advancing the task. Assignment requires **capability** (office.action-domain covers task.requires), **authority** (office permitted to accept this work), **capacity** (office has bandwidth).

**Cross-axis extractions**:
- tasks an officer takes → [work-axis](work-axis.md) via assignments
- skills an officer uses → [capability-axis](capability-axis.md) via `uses-skill:`
- lessons learned by an officer → [memory-axis](memory-axis.md) via memory records
- events produced by officer action → [work-axis](work-axis.md) via session/event records

Office records are dense by design — they declare the normative structure. Officer records are thin — they just record who currently fills which office.

See also: [system-axes](system-axes.md), [work-axis](work-axis.md), [capability-axis](capability-axis.md).
"}

id: observation-axis
title: "Observation axis — analyses, decisions, directives, claims about state"
type: term
defines: observation-axis
date-created: 2026-04-05
description: "The axis of time-indexed witnessed claims. Analyses observe; decisions settle; directives instruct; research-notes survey. All make claims ABOUT records on other axes at a given time."
instance-of: categorical-axis
part-of: system-axes
objects: [analysis, decision, directive, research-note, idea]
internal-morphisms: [supersedes, builds-on, cites, settled-by]
structure: "time-indexed comma category over records on other axes; each observation points at what it witnesses and when"
cross-axis-morphisms:
  to-work: [analyzes, decides-about, directs]
  to-predication: [establishes-term, settles, constrains-vocabulary]
  to-agency: [attributed-to]
  to-capability: [identifies-capability-gap]
  to-memory: [produces-instinct, generates-lesson]
math-lineage: "comma category over state; Luhmann second-order observation; double-loop learning (Argyris); libraries' decision-record tradition"
related: [system-axes, work-axis, predication-axis]
readiness: shaped
---

Objects on this axis are time-indexed witnessed claims about the state of the rest of the system at a given moment. **Analyses** diagnose; **decisions** settle choices with rationale; **directives** issue instructions (usually captain-sourced); **research-notes** survey external material to ground internal choices.

Unlike work-axis records (which commit to future action) or predication-axis records (which define vocabulary), observation-axis records are *past-tense*: they record what was seen, what was decided, what was directed — at a time. They are the system's audit-trail for *thinking*, not for *doing*.

Internal morphisms:
- **supersedes** — observation B replaces observation A (captain directive revised; decision reversed)
- **builds-on** — B uses A's finding as a premise
- **cites** — B references A as evidence
- **settled-by** — a predication-axis term was made definite via this decision

**Prose IS the content** on this axis. Unlike work/agency/capability axes where bodies compress to minimal prose, analyses carry their findings AS PROSE because the finding is discursive. A decision's rationale is irreducibly narrative. Compress scaffolding, not content.

**Cross-axis extractions** FROM observation records:
- a commitment proposed by the analysis → [work-axis](work-axis.md) plan (don't mix analysis + plan in one file)
- a term proposed by the decision → [predication-axis](predication-axis.md) term
- implementation required by the directive → [capability-axis](capability-axis.md) skill/command

**Cross-axis extractions INTO observation records:** when a work-axis plan accumulates architectural rationale, trade-off analysis, or historical context, extract it to an analysis record referenced via `analyzed-by:` on the plan.

See also: [system-axes](system-axes.md), [work-axis](work-axis.md), [predication-axis](predication-axis.md).
"}

id: capability-axis
title: "Capability axis — executable terms (skills, commands, hooks, agents)"
type: term
defines: capability-axis
date-created: 2026-04-05
description: "The axis of code-as-data: executable procedures that agents invoke to act on the graph, the filesystem, or external services. Each capability is a term whose body is executable."
instance-of: categorical-axis
part-of: system-axes
objects: [skill, command, hook, agent, rule, spec-of-executable]
internal-morphisms: [composes, depends-on, triggers, subsumes]
structure: "algebra of effectful processes; composable by call-graph; each capability has declared inputs, outputs, preconditions, effects"
cross-axis-morphisms:
  to-work: [produces-event, advances-task, creates-record]
  to-predication: [grounded-in-term, implements-invariant]
  to-agency: [dispatched-by, permitted-for-office]
  to-observation: [produces-analysis, logs-event]
  to-memory: [triggers-instinct, observes-pattern]
math-lineage: "algebra of effectful computation; command pattern (GoF); MUD driver architecture (LPMud); MCP typed tools; library/.../computing/texts/"
related: [system-axes, agency-axis, predication-axis]
readiness: shaped
---

Objects on this axis are executable. A **skill** is a bundle of instructions an agent loads to perform work of a specific kind. A **command** is a named procedure with argument schema. A **hook** fires on an event and may mutate or block. An **agent** is a dispatchable worker-role. A **rule** fires on graph change and produces side-effects.

Each capability declares: inputs (arguments), outputs (results), preconditions (what must be true to run), effects (what it changes), and its grounding term (what predicate-definition it implements).

**Composition** on this axis: a skill composes commands; a hook triggers skills; an agent uses skills; a rule fires commands. The call-graph among capabilities IS the algebra — running skill X invokes commands A, B, C, each of which may invoke further primitives.

**Cross-axis extractions**:
- the work the capability advances → [work-axis](work-axis.md) via events produced
- the term the capability implements → [predication-axis](predication-axis.md) via `grounded-in-term:`
- the office authorized to run it → [agency-axis](agency-axis.md) via `permitted-for-office:`
- the pattern it detects → [memory-axis](memory-axis.md) via `observes-pattern:`

Capability records have two bodies: the **definition** (what the capability does, grounded in a term) and the **implementation** (the code). In FARS the implementation is usually a separate file (a `.js` or `.md` with instructions) referenced by the capability record's frontmatter.

See also: [system-axes](system-axes.md), [agency-axis](agency-axis.md), [predication-axis](predication-axis.md).
"}

Objects on this axis are executable. A **skill** is a bundle of instructions an agent loads to perform work of a specific kind. A **command** is a named procedure with argument schema. A **hook** fires on an event and may mutate or block. An **agent** is a dispatchable worker-role. A **rule** fires on graph change and produces side-effects.

Each capability declares: inputs (arguments), outputs (results), preconditions (what must be true to run), effects (what it changes), and its grounding term (what predicate-definition it implements).

id: work-domain-external-sources
title: "External disciplinary sources for work-domain terms"
type: research-note
date-created: 2026-04-01
serves: work-domain-layer-separation
---

External-discipline sources for grounding the general work-domain terms being written per the work-domain-layer-separation plan.

## Skill

- **Dreyfus & Dreyfus (1980/1986), *Mind Over Machine*** — five-stage skill acquisition: novice (context-free rules), advanced beginner (situational patterns), competent (deliberate plans), proficient (intuition, own rules), expert (fluid unconscious action). Skill is NOT a rule — starts as rule-following, compiles into automatic performance.
- **ACT-R (Anderson, 1983/1993)** — skill as procedural memory: condition→action production rules firing without deliberation.
- **Schön (1983), *The Reflective Practitioner*** — professional knowledge is reflection-in-action, not technical rationality. "Know more than they can put into words." Connects skill to practice.
- **Robotics skill libraries** — parameterized reusable capability composed by higher-level planner.

## Work unit

- **Annett & Duncan (1967), Hierarchical Task Analysis** — task decomposes into operations (atomic units) with inputs, action, outputs. Decomposition stops when p×c (probability × cost of failure) falls below threshold.
- **PMI/PMBOK, Work Breakdown Structure** — "deliverable-oriented hierarchical decomposition." Work package = lowest WBS level, estimable/schedulable/trackable.

## Workflow

- **Workflow Management Coalition (WfMC, 1995)** — "automation of a business process… documents, information or tasks passed from one participant to another for action, according to procedural rules."
- **BPMN (OMG, 2004/2011)** — standard graphical notation for business processes: sequences, gateways, events, parallel paths. ISO 19510.
- **Petri nets (Petri, 1962)** — bipartite graph of places and transitions. Workflow soundness = every case that starts eventually completes. Standard formal model; CS, not FARS.

## Plan

- **Bratman (1987), *Intention, Plans, and Practical Reason*** — plans as commitments: normatively binding intentions, not just sequences. Three roles: temporal coordination, social coordination, nesting. Partial plans are the norm; reconsideration requires reasons.
- **STRIPS (Fikes & Nilsson, 1971)** — first formal planning language.
- **PDDL (Ghallab et al., 1998)** — standard planning language.
- **McAllester & Rosenblitt (1991)** — partial-order planning: commit only to what must happen before what, not to total sequence.

## Project

- **PMI/PMBOK** — "temporary endeavor undertaken to create a unique product, service, or result." Bounded scope, defined end state. Distinguished from program (related projects) and portfolio (aligned to strategy).
- **Annett & Duncan → PMI hierarchy** — program → project → work packages → activities. Maps to repo's endeavor → project → task → work-unit.

## Objective

- **Doran (1981)** — SMART criteria: Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, Time-bounded.
- **Grove/Doerr, OKR** — Objectives (qualitative direction) + Key Results (quantitative milestones).

title: "Progressive automation — settlement path, per-agent demotions, dispatch flow"
type: analysis
date-created: 2026-04-04

Policy 001: every task completion should encode itself so a less capable agent can do it next time. The offices-as-fuzzy-cells analysis identified 7 offices at near-F3 formality whose work is deterministic given inputs. We are wrapping parameterized commands in inference agents. A first-officer `harness-cleaner` dispatch spawns a sonnet subagent (~4K system prompt), which runs the same grep/glob/read pipeline every time, formats markdown, returns. ~10K tokens for work a 50-line script could do.

## The settlement path: agent → skill → tool → hook

| Level | When | Permission | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| Agent | irreducibly fuzzy, needs judgment/synthesis/multi-step reasoning | subagent spawn, user approval per tool | high (~10K+ tokens) |
| Skill | structured procedure, fixed steps needing inference to parameterize | loaded into calling agent's context | medium (~2K tokens) |
| Tool | deterministic given parameters, node script | runs as calling process, no approval | low (~100 tokens per call) |
| Hook | triggered by events, no dispatch needed | async or blocking on event | zero dispatch cost |

## Wave 1 — read-only reporters (lowest risk, highest savings)

**1. harness-cleaner → harness-audit.js** — sonnet agent runs fixed grep/count pipeline classifying UNUSED/STALE/DUPLICATE. Node script takes `--scope agents|skills|hooks|commands|all`. Agent prompt IS the spec.

**2. graph-analyst → query-library-graph.js `report` subcommand** — already exists as a tool; the agent just picks which query. Add `report` for common queries (coverage, gaps, orphans, stats). Cartographer subsumes graph-analyst for anything needing judgment.

**3. docs-lookup → library-search.js** — agent runs three-step fallback (graph query → filename glob → content grep). Node script implements the same pipeline. Researcher subsumes for interpretation.

## Wave 2 — deterministic producers (write files)

**4. doc-updater → update-indexes.js + hook** — regenerate indexes from filesystem reality; could become PostToolUse hook on Write/Edit. Writes are a pure function of filesystem.

**5. quartermaster → resource-report.js** — composes existing tools (graph stats, events, session metrics); threshold-based flagging is already formal. Low risk (read-only despite Bash access).

**6. bookkeeper → ledger.js (extend finance-report.js)** — records transactions, runs trial balances. Double-entry invariant (debits=credits) is algebraically checkable. Moderate risk — writes to ledger but with strict rules.

## Wave 3 — pattern detection (needs care)

**7. observer → pattern-detector.js + hook integration** — sequence analysis on observation JSONL with configurable thresholds (3+ → instinct). Confidence scoring is already a formal function. Moderate risk — current system works; implementation needs care against false positives.

## What stays as agents (irreducibly fuzzy)

| Office | Why stays | Formality ceiling |
|---|---|---|
| architect | system design needs contextual judgment | F1 site, F1 production |
| researcher | reading comprehension + synthesis across sources | F1/F1 |
| triage-processor | unstructured → structured needs editorial judgment | F0 recognition |
| writer | prose quality not formalizable | F1 production |
| planner | decomposition of novel requests | F1 recognition |
| chief-of-staff | cross-domain synthesis | F1 production |
| operations-officer | work management prioritization | F2 judgment-heavy |
| helmsman | dispatch routing matching | F2 context-dependent |

**Premise.** Every 561 record is a message. Every mutation is a message. Every observation is a received message. The event-jsonl-format spec already carries messaging fields (`audience`, `channel`, `body`) and double-entry accounting fields (`sourceAccount`/`destinationAccount`/`resource`/`commodity`/`quantity`). Records-as-objects is a view; records-as-messages is the substrate that subsumes it.

The adjoint paper's history monoid T IS a message-log. The fiber functor H_t IS the channel schema at time t. The nucleus operations ARE delivery-and-settlement operators. The math is already messaging; the records haven't caught up.

**The six inner axes** (work/predication/agency/observation/capability/memory) classify message **payloads**, not free-standing objects. Messaging is the ambient substrate; axes live inside its envelope. This subsumes: temporality (send-time is inherent), provenance (sender+reference-chain), boundary/recipient (sender/receiver poles), the attempted boundary-duality (dissolves — every message crosses boundaries by construction).

**Required records (each its own record-type):**

- **channel** — one per named channel: declares schema, delivery-semantics, subscribers. Currently implicit (bridge/fleet/engineering/failures as constants); must become explicit records.
- **message-envelope** — uniform frontmatter carried by every record: sender, channel, timestamp, receivers, lifecycle. Current records carry some (date-created, status) but not others (sender, receivers).
- **witness** — certification of another message. Frontmatter: `witnesses: <msg-id>`, `verdict: {acknowledged, acted-on, refuted, superseded}`, `witnessed-by: <session>`.
- **subscription** — declares a receiver's interest in a channel. Frontmatter: `subscriber: <office>`, `channel: <channel-id>`, `filter: <pattern>`.
- **delivery-state-log** — append-only record of per-(message, receiver) state transitions. Could be a sub-channel of events.

**Connection to existing library terms:** channel.md (medium with capacity/bandwidth/noise), witness.md (constructive proof — specific object satisfying existential claim), event.md (Kim/Davidson/Whitehead on event individuation).

**Open questions:**
- does `message-id` derive from content-hash (content-addressed) or from (sender, channel, time) triple?
- how do channels federate when FARS instances talk to each other (ActivityPub-style? Matrix-style? Custom)?
- what's the minimum subscription-pattern language (exact-channel-match? glob? predicate-filter?)
- how does the bilattice value interact with delivery lifecycle (can a message be delivered with confidence ⊥?)

For a distributed heterogeneous agentic system at nation-scale, message-passing is the primary concern: how do agents coordinate when they run in different processes, at different times, under different models, across different sites? Real-world messaging systems have solved slices of this problem. Each brings a pattern the 561 system can adopt.

## Apache Kafka — log-based messaging

Kafka stores messages as an **append-only log partitioned across brokers**. Producers write to topics; consumers read by offset, replay at will. The log IS the state — downstream systems derive their view by consuming the log from offset 0. Retention is time-bounded (hours to forever). Ordering is guaranteed within a partition, not across.

**Pattern:** event-log-as-source-of-truth. Derived state is always rebuildable from replaying the log. 561's `events.jsonl` already implements this pattern in miniature — one JSONL file as the append-only log, knowledge graph as derived view.

**Applicable:** the entire EAVT graph is Kafka-style: knowledge-graph.json is consumers' materialized view of events.jsonl. Multi-log partitioning could enable per-channel append-only files (plans-log, terms-log, decisions-log) without a single contention point.

## NATS — subject-based pub/sub

NATS is a lightweight broker with **hierarchical subjects** (`agents.researcher.dispatched`) and wildcard subscriptions (`agents.*.dispatched`). Messages are typed by subject; subscribers express interest via subject patterns. Default delivery is at-most-once (fast, no persistence); JetStream adds durable streams.

**Pattern:** hierarchical channel naming + subscriber-pattern matching. Channels form a tree; subscriptions are cut-patterns on the tree.

**Applicable:** 561's implicit channels (bridge, fleet, engineering, failures) could be expressed as NATS-style subjects (`ops.planning.dispatched`, `ops.engineering.failed`). Office subscriptions could be declared as patterns, making subscription routing mechanical.

## RabbitMQ — AMQP exchanges and routing

RabbitMQ decouples publishers from queues via **exchanges**: publishers send to an exchange, which routes to queues by type (fanout, direct, topic, headers). Consumers bind queues to exchanges with routing keys. Messages acknowledge explicitly; rejected messages retry or dead-letter.

**Pattern:** routing as a first-class concern, separate from delivery. A message's destination is computed from its routing-key + exchange-binding, not baked into the message.

**Applicable:** 561's dispatch-routing is currently implicit (first-officer computes which office matches a task). An AMQP-style exchange would make routing rules explicit and queryable — task.requires routes through a binding that selects offices, rather than inference.

## ActivityPub — federated social messaging

ActivityPub uses **HTTP POST to each actor's `inbox`**, with actor profiles served at stable URLs. Activities (`Create`, `Follow`, `Like`, `Announce`) are typed JSON-LD objects. Federation works via HTTP signatures: server A delivers to server B by signing and POST-ing. No central authority. Each server maintains its own state; federation is eventually consistent.

**Pattern:** federation through typed HTTP endpoints with cryptographic provenance. Each participant is sovereign; federation is optional and asymmetric (you can follow without being followed back).
